channel.title: Jasper's Agent Watch
channel.description: Daily notes on AI agents and agent context: fast-growing GitHub projects, papers, and why they spread.

item.title: ⚠️ Some social platform engagement data is missing today, so the related numbers are for reference only.
item.description:
• GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance grew fastest today at +2,223/day. Chrome published it, and its Show HN post (11-10) has 448 points and 146 comments, the most discussion of any project on the list.
  • Many growth-list entries are skill and rule packs that bolt onto an agent: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter, Leonxlnx/taste-skill, affaan-m/ECC, DietrichGebert/ponytail, cloudflare/security-audit-skill and NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator.
  • Two interfaces for managing several coding agents at once, pingdotgg/t3code (+1,331/day) and stablyai/orca (+1,019/day), both pitch "use the subscriptions you already have."
  • The two biggest single-project videos are Outskill's tutorial on morluto/rea (▶471,410 views) and Rob Shocks' Orca video (▶78,911 views, 11-14). X engagement data for both projects is missing.
  • Today's HN agent threads cluster around three topics: Windows 11 collecting telemetry on which coding agents you use (685 points, 550 comments), verification (the Claude Code team on it), and keeping credentials away from agents.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-17
item.description:
• Memory is still the most concentrated topic. MIRIX-2.0 went from 👍26 in the 11-16 report to 👍52, with its repo at ⭐3488. It is the only rising memory paper today.
  • Two new papers question whether experience or memory always helps. Experience Rot finds that after a tool is silently changed, agents carrying experience do worse than novices. Continual-ARC finds that most harness-based persistence methods learn less than the floor of simply caching demonstrations.
  • Self-evolution and memory writes now pass through gates. FGSE tests memory updates as hypotheses, EGE runs an independent audit before adoption, and G-CAST switches checkpoints under control. All three appeared on the same day.
  • Tool and context cost: Beyond Plain MCP measures code mode at 70–90% fewer tokens than plain MCP, and EfficientSkill prunes skill instructions to cut output tokens by up to 80%.
  • The highest-upvoted hot and new papers (Envisioning Agentic Robotics 👍123, Gamer 👍116, Sage 👍81) are mostly model or robotics work. Pure Agent Context papers have low upvotes.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-16
item.description:
• Memory papers still compete on LoCoMo and LongMemEval. MIRIX-2.0 has the most upvotes in the hot list (26) and its repo has ⭐3472.
  • A controlled comparison of compressed memory against raw text: on LoCoMo, 2611.09807 finds compression wins when the answer is a value and loses when the answer needs the original wording.
  • Memory security and deletion are becoming their own topic. MemoryDojo tests memory poisoning, and LinEra does provable memory erasure.
  • The top new papers are Envisioning Agentic Robotics (👍107), Gamer (👍86) and VibePrevisBench (👍82). Only Gamer's context management touches Agent Context.
  • On long-horizon evaluation, Infrathon keeps climbing (👍56). Model rankings change with evaluation time.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-15
item.description:
• The hot list is cold today. The top Agent Context paper has only 👍8. Memory papers lead: multi-user memory isolation (MixUA), multimodal memory (HiVe-Mem) and agents organizing their own memory (SoMem).
  • Memory systems are starting to ask who can read what. MixUA scopes experience by user, agent and global, and tests for privacy leaks. MemoryDojo tests memory poisoning.
  • Handing experience from one run to the next is now a training target. EHRL uses RL to train playbook writing inside the ACE framework.
  • Infrathon is the only rising paper today, up from 👍25 to 👍52. In long-horizon evaluation, model rankings change with the length of the budget.
  • The new list is empty, so there is no "announced last night" picks today.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-13
item.description:
• Context cost is the clearest thread today. SparseRead has the most upvotes (👍21) of the Agent Context papers on the hot list. It adds a read-control layer that cuts total tokens by up to 92.9%.
  • Most of the new long-horizon context-management papers are in the New section. Folio folds context at multiple resolutions and can restore it. HiVe-Mem does multimodal memory. MemCredit picks memories by decision utility. MAPE searches for memory designs through program evolution.
  • KV cache is getting attention in agent settings. Octopus treats KV as shared state across branches, Nebula does position-independent caching, and HeMeR reuses KV for embodied agents.
  • Evaluation and training environments lead the hot list: SteerDistill (👍34) and Embodied First Exam (👍28). Security has two threads: memory poisoning (MemoryDojo) and authorization drift (ADB).
  • The top New papers by upvotes are PhysLoop (👍36) and Actor, Judge, or Teacher? (👍29). PhysLoop has nothing to do with Agent Context. It just has "harness" in the name.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-12
item.description:
• Memory reliability is the main thread. WikiTrace links each stored lesson back to the raw trajectory, to cut cases where memory makes an agent worse than having none (HF 👍60, the hottest Agent Context paper today).
  • Many papers cut the cost of context compression and reading. SparseRead saves up to 92.9% of tokens, SumOne cuts inference cost by about 75–78%, and SpecCompact is 2.04–5.63× faster.
  • Inference infrastructure is being designed around agent context and KV cache. Evolving Infra uses agent context-management signals to decide KV cache eviction and transfer.
  • Harness and embodied-agent work is heating up. Embodied First Exam (👍27, GitHub ★263), Auriga and RoboScript all have coding agents controlling robots.
  • Benchmarks are moving toward safety and compliance. Authorization drift (Authorization Drift), reward hacking (Coding or Cheating?), fraud (FraudBench) and scraping compliance (ScrapeBench) all appeared on the same day.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-11
item.description:
• Few hot-list papers are about memory or compression. The new context papers are in the "new" batch: WikiTrace (memory with links back to evidence), FGSE (try to falsify a memory before writing it), CAMP-II (files as memory, trained with on-policy distillation), TreeAgent (memory for long structured inputs) and SHADOWPREFILL (pre-warming the KV cache for model switches).
  • The highest-voted hot paper is Flide (👍35, GitHub ⭐430, OmniJev/Flide). It does exact state forking for agent decision models, reusing prefixes instead of recomputing them.
  • The only paper still climbing is Hao Fei's Cognitive Symbionts (👍105, 7 days on the list). It is still a vision paper with no experiments, and it has been on the list for several days (see the 11-07, 11-08 and 11-10 reports and the W45 weekly).
  • A small trend: memory writes now get checked first. WikiTrace and FGSE both target bad experiences polluting memory.
  • The other-agent papers are mostly benchmarks and training infrastructure: Infrathon, Longtail-SWE, AutoVend, ReproBridge and PCBRouteAgent.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-10
item.description:
• Context papers on the hot list cluster around three themes: compressing tool observations (Coca-Cola), reliability after compression or memory updates (ARCBench, StateGraph), and KV cache behavior in agent serving (Metastability, PARC).
  • ARCBench finds compression rarely deletes rules. Most violations happen while the rule is still in the compressed history, and compaction runs that keep the rules violate them at more than double the rate of full history.
  • Two empirical papers cast doubt on self-evolving harnesses. Beneath the Surface and Continual evolution both find that rising scores don't mean reliable improvement. In the latter, SWE-Bench falls from 94.0% to 32.0% after evolving on a new task.
  • Among last night's arXiv papers, memory systems (MIRIX-2.0, SoMem) and agent-side KV cache management (Evolving Infra, VerKV, Hibana, Flide) show up together.
  • The only rising paper is Cognitive Symbionts, a position paper by Hao Fei. It went from 0 to 👍104 in 7 days, the most upvotes of any agent paper in today's data.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-09
item.description:
• No breakout this edition. The top status=hot paper is LongBanana (👍24). From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts leads the overall board with 👍120, but it is a rising paper and a vision piece with no experiments.
  • Context compression is moving from text to latent space. Coca-Cola compresses tool outputs into latent tokens and cuts token use by 70.01% to 89.24%. SwarmEvolve has agents communicate by passing KV cache.
  • Several agent papers center on KV cache and prefix caching. The SIMPLE law quantifies the energy cost of agent requests. In the New list, Nebula and DARIC both reuse KV cache.
  • Two papers look critically at self-evolving harnesses. Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting? (SWE-Bench 94.0% to 32.0%) is on the hot list, and Beneath the Surface is in New. Both find that a higher benchmark score does not mean a more reliable agent.
  • Memory safety and trade-offs are getting attention. New has MemoryDojo, a memory-poisoning benchmark, and a paired comparison of conversation-memory compaction vs RAG.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context Papers · 2026-11-08
item.description:
• Context compression is following two routes. One rewrites reasoning history into compact state records (Reasoning History Compaction, 👍13). The other compresses tool outputs into latent tokens (Coca-Cola, tokens down 70.01%–89.24%).
  • Switching between tasks is now a measurable failure point for context management. Switch-SWE found that interleaving unfinished tasks cut the solve rate of 7 coding agents by 11.5 points on average. A context-management plugin recovered 5.5–15.5 points.
  • Continually evolving harnesses forget. Meta-Harness dropped from 94.0% to 32.0% on SWE-Bench (see section 2).
  • Guardrails are the most crowded theme among the other Agent papers: Caper and LeanGuard both intercept tool calls before they execute.
  • Cognitive Symbionts went from 40 to 114 upvotes. It is still a vision paper with no experiments (see the 11-07 report).

item.title: Agent & Agent Context Papers · 2026-11-07
item.description:
• Harnesses are the most concentrated topic today. Harness-S (ranked first), the continual-evolution forgetting study, RoboArchitect and TinyAstral all work on evolving or transferring an agent's harness (the scaffolding around the model).
  • Continual evolution forgets, with numbers: Meta-Harness on SWE-Bench fell from 94.0% to 32.0%, a 66% relative drop.
  • Context management now has measurable gains. Switch-SWE's task-switching plugin improves OpenCode by 5.5–15.5 percentage points, and rewriting reasoning history can cut agent cost.
  • KV cache shows up in two directions. SwarmEvolve has agents communicate through it, and the SIMPLE law measures cached agentic requests at 4.8x the energy of ordinary ones.
  • The position paper Cognitive Symbionts has the most upvotes in the context/memory group (👍40), but it is a vision paper with no experiments.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-06
item.description:
• Context management is moving from compressing text to passing KV state in latent space. Octopus (a DAG of forked KV states), SwarmEvolve (agents pass KV cache to each other) and CacheGraft (documents pre-encoded as KV) all appeared on the same day, in the New section.
  • The harness is now an optimization target. Harness-S (👍51 in New, the day's highest), ParetoSaddler and RoboArchitect all improve or evolve harnesses automatically.
  • Memory work is getting deeper. EvoMemState turns memory from independent facts into facts with relational state, and MemSteer generates supervision from user histories to tune memory design.
  • Long-horizon context problems now have a direct benchmark. Switch-SWE tests whether an agent recovers after switching tasks, and its context-management plugin adds 5.5 to 15.5 percentage points.
  • Many benchmark papers (FrontierPhysics, MCPHallu and others) conclude that frontier agents still have clear gaps.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-04
item.description:
• The most-liked papers are a survey and a harness paper. Advances in Agentic Computer Graphics leads with 👍127. CoworkOS has 👍96 and 104 stars on its code.
  • Several empirical studies look at memory and context management: what happens after a task switch (Switch-SWE), what a compressed memory should keep (Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong), and when memory helps at all (What Is This Memory Useful For?, in the New section).
  • Two papers keep history or output outside the agent's context. SWE-Trail uses history only to steer data collection. GeoFaham (New) stores full outputs outside the context and passes only identifiers and summaries.
  • Harnesses are now a research subject: verification strategy (Rethinking Verification), automatic harness evolution (RoboArchitect, ParetoSaddler, EvoGroup), and how skills evolve on GitHub (84,200 skills).
  • Computer-use agent (CUA) training loops cluster on the list. CUA-Master scores 80.2 on OSWorld Verified, and NorthCUA appears in the same window.
